tasks.short: Observe and caution children petting and feeding animals.

steps.what: Observe children petting and feeding animals in the designated areas.
inputs: the children in the designated area

steps.what: Caution those children so the humans and the animals stay safe.

tasks.design: The caretaker watches the children and the animals in the designated area and cautions the children in the moment. No note and no model sees that moment or speaks the caution.
tasks.previous_blocker: The risk is in how a child and an animal are behaving right now, which is visible only in the area.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new is required. The caretaker already does this by watching and speaking.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing a child too close, or an animal that has had enough, and saying the caution in time, stays with the caretaker.
tasks.human_edge: Judging the child and the animal together, and speaking before either is hurt.
tasks.altitude: The week does not change. The caretaker still observes every designated area and still cautions the children.

reach.task: Mark which areas are designated for children to pet and feed
reach.learn: To say which animals are in those areas and which are not

evidence.claim: Watching children pet and feed animals, and cautioning them, happens in the area. A note cannot see the moment. Model knowledge.
Examining an animal and prescribing or giving treatment are reserved for admitted persons such as registered vets. This task is watching and cautioning, not treatment.

assumptions: The boundary is one designated area and the children in it. Observing and cautioning each keep their full time.
There is no structured input and no machine action. Nothing sends a caution, raises an alert, or fills a form.
The caretaker adds no recurring chore. Upkeep on this task is zero.
unknowns: Whether the centre has areas marked for children, or the caretaker decides the boundary each visit.
research_questions: How often is the caution a standing rule of the area, and how often does it turn on what the caretaker sees in this child or this animal?

incremental.description: The caretaker adds no recurring chore. Observing and cautioning stay the whole task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Observing the children and the animals, and cautioning them, both stay in the area at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the grooming notes that match these pets before the discussion.
inputs: grooming card when the senior caretaker has written one

steps.what: Discuss with clients their pets' grooming needs.
inputs: what the client says about the pet
outputs: the grooming needs agreed in the discussion

tasks.design: The senior caretaker keeps a grooming card: species, coat, what the salon does, and what it does not do. The caretaker reads that card, or the salon list when a row is missing, then discusses the pet's needs with the client. The discussion stays in the room.
tasks.previous_blocker: What the salon will groom sat in a list, so each client started as a search.
tasks.enabler_now: The senior caretaker already knows the salon's grooming list. Writing it once on a card needs no new system and no model.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing what this client wants, looking at this pet, and agreeing what the salon will do, stays with the caretaker.
tasks.human_edge: Agreeing a grooming need that matches this pet and what the client can accept.
tasks.altitude: Finding the salon list is shorter when the card is current. The caretaker still discusses every pet with the client.

reach.task: Keep the grooming card for each species and coat
reach.learn: To name what the salon does and what it refuses, and to change the row when the service changes

evidence.claim: A grooming discussion is with the client, about this pet. A card of what the salon does can shorten the search. It does not hold the discussion. Model knowledge.
Examining an animal and prescribing or giving treatment are reserved for admitted persons such as registered vets. Discussing grooming needs is not that act.

assumptions: The boundary is one client and one pet. The discussion keeps its full time.

Grooming card fields are species, coat, what the salon does, and what it does not do. The producer is the senior caretaker, when a service changes. If a row is missing, the caretaker reads the salon list inside the lookup.
The card does not speak to the client, send a message, or raise an alert. The caretaker does not diagnose the pet in this task.
Card upkeep is the senior caretaker's 1 hour per 100 caretaker hours on this task. The caretaker's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether a senior caretaker keeps the salon list, or each caretaker holds their own.
How often the discussion turns into a health question that must go to a vet.
research_questions: Of the grooming discussions here, how many follow the salon list, and how many turn on a coat or a request the list does not name?

incremental.description: The caretaker adds no recurring chore. Reading the card is the lookup step.
The senior caretaker updates the grooming card when a species, a coat rule, or a refused service changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the card has no row for this coat, the caretaker reads the salon list inside the lookup. The discussion stays at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Order, unload, and store feed and supplies.

steps.what: See which feed and supplies are low.
inputs: the feed and supplies on the shelf
outputs: the feed and supplies that are low

steps.what: Read the pack and the supplier for that feed and those supplies.
inputs: the feed and supplies that are low
item card when the stores colleague has written one
outputs: the pack and the supplier to use

steps.what: Order that feed and those supplies from the supplier.
inputs: the pack and the supplier to use

steps.what: Unload the feed and supplies that arrive.
Store the feed and supplies in their place.

tasks.design: The stores colleague keeps an item card: item, species, pack, and supplier. The caretaker sees what is low, reads pack and supplier from the card or from the shelf label when a row is missing, and orders by phone or on paper. Unloading and storing stay physical. Nothing sends the order.
tasks.previous_blocker: Pack size and supplier sat on old delivery notes, so each order started as a search.
tasks.enabler_now: The stores colleague already knows the usual pack and supplier. Writing them once on a card needs no new system.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing what is actually low, placing the order, unloading the delivery, and putting it away stay with the caretaker.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing what is on the shelf, and refusing to order a quantity they did not see.
tasks.altitude: Finding pack and supplier is shorter when the card is current. The caretaker still sees what is low, still places the order, and still unloads and stores.

reach.task: Keep item, species, pack and supplier on the feed card
reach.learn: To change the row when the supplier or the pack changes, and not to write the quantity on hand

evidence.claim: Ordering feed is seeing what is low and telling the supplier. A card can hold pack and supplier. It does not see the shelf, place the order, unload, or store. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The boundary is one store room and one order. Seeing what is low, placing the order, unloading, and storing each keep their full time.

Item card fields are item, species, pack, and supplier. The producer is the stores colleague, when a supplier or a pack changes. The quantity on hand is what the caretaker sees, not a field on the card. If a row is missing, the caretaker reads the shelf label inside the lookup.
The caretaker places the order by phone or on paper. Nothing sends the order, fills a form, or raises an alert from a low shelf.
Card upkeep is the stores colleague's 1.5 hours per 100 caretaker hours on this task. The caretaker's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether a stores colleague keeps supplier names, or the caretaker is the only person who knows them.
How often the supplier will not take a phone or paper order.
research_questions: Of the feed orders here, how many use a known pack and supplier, and how many need a new supplier the card does not name?

incremental.description: The caretaker adds no recurring chore. Reading the card is the lookup step.
The stores colleague updates the item card when the pack or the supplier changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the card has no supplier, the caretaker reads the shelf label inside the lookup. Seeing what is low, ordering, unloading, and storing stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read which pet food and supplies fit this animal.
inputs: product card when the shop lead has written one
outputs: the pet food and supplies that fit

steps.what: Sell the pet food and supplies to this client.
inputs: the pet food and supplies that fit

tasks.design: The shop lead keeps a product card: species, item, size, and price. The caretaker reads that card, or the shelf label when a row is missing, then sells to the client in person, including taking payment. The sale stays with the caretaker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Which food fits a species, and its price, sat on shelf labels, so each sale started as a search.
tasks.enabler_now: The shop lead already sets the species, the size, and the price. Writing them once on a card needs no new system.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing what the client wants, matching it to this animal, and taking the payment stay with the caretaker.
tasks.human_edge: Selling the item that fits this animal, and refusing one the note does not name for that species.
tasks.altitude: Finding species, size, and price is shorter when the card is current. The caretaker still sells, and still takes the payment.

reach.task: Keep species, item, size and price on the product card
reach.learn: To date the price and to strike an item the shop no longer sells

evidence.claim: Selling pet food is talking with the client and taking payment. A card of species, size, and price can shorten the search. It does not make the sale. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The boundary is one client and one animal. Selling, including taking payment, keeps its full time.
Product card fields are species, item, size, and price. The producer is the shop lead, when a price or a size changes. If a row is missing, the caretaker reads the shelf label inside the lookup.
The card does not sell, take payment, send a receipt, or raise an alert.
Card upkeep is the shop lead's 1.5 hours per 100 caretaker hours on this task. The caretaker's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether a shop lead keeps prices, or the caretaker reads only shelf labels.
How often a sale is for an animal whose species is not on the card.
research_questions: Of the pet-food sales here, how many are a listed species and price, and how many need a label the card does not hold?

incremental.description: The caretaker adds no recurring chore. Reading the card is the lookup step.
The shop lead updates the product card when a species, a size, or a price changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the card has no row, the caretaker reads the shelf label inside the lookup. Selling and taking payment stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The caretaker still watches and cautions children in the area, still discusses grooming with the client, still sees what is low, places the order, unloads and stores, and still sells in person. A current card only shortens finding a salon rule, a pack and supplier, or a price.
reach: A kennel supervisor learns to mark which areas are designated for children before the caretaker observes them.
A senior caretaker learns to name species, coat, and what the salon refuses before a grooming discussion.
A stores colleague learns to keep item, pack, and supplier, and not to write the quantity the caretaker must see.
A shop lead learns to date the price on the product card before a sale.
skills_to_grow: Open the salon list, the shelf label, or the class note when the card has no row.
Order only the quantity they saw, and do not treat the card as a count.
Keep grooming talk and a sale out of diagnosis, and send a health question to a vet.
role.ambitious_version: The caretaker still watches, discusses, orders, unloads, stores, and sells. The cards do not caution, discuss, order, or sell.
